local_articles.title: UAE condemns alleged attack on ADNOC-linked vessel in Strait of Hormuz
local_articles.snippet: ABU DHABI: The United Arab Emirates condemned what it described as an Iranian attack on a vessel linked to ADNOC as it transited the Strait of Hormuz, saying no injuries were reported. The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement Saturday that the incident violated a UN Security Council resolution affirming freedom of navigation and rejecting attacks on commercial vessels or obstruction of international maritime routes. The ministry accused Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps of using the strategic waterway as a tool of economic coercion and said such acts threatened regional stability and global energy security. The UAE called on Iran to halt what it called unprovoked attacks and to ensure the Strait of Hormuz remains fully open to safeguard regional security and global trade.

questions.title: Who will be the first major Ukrainian political figure to publicly call for wartime elections following Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion?
questions.background: Ukrainian law bars elections during wartime. The presidential election has been postponed under continuing martial law, although Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s presidential term ended in May 2024.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements corroborated by reliable contemporaneous news reporting. Qualifying Event : Identify the person credited in reliable reporting with the first public call by a major Ukrainian political figure since Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion to resume national elections while the war continues. A call solely for elections after the war ends does not qualify. Resolution Timing : Resolve when the qualifying statement becomes public, provided this occurs by August 31, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The politician’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-08-12 refresh (first update since June 24) incorporating July-August Ukrainian political upheaval: (1) Volodymyr Zelenskyy rises to #1 (0.16 -> 0.21) after Ukrainska Pravda (July) and NV.ua (Aug 8) reported Zelenskyy privately told Ambassador Valerii Zaluzhnyi in Kyiv that 'most likely we will have to hold elections this autumn' citing a frontline window and social consolidation, before publicly denying plans on July 2 and launching a sweeping mid-July cabinet reshuffle ('changing its political strategy'). (4) Petro Poroshenko trims (0.22 -> 0.16): still leader of the largest parliamentary opposition party (European Solidarity) with strong anti-Zelenskyy incentives, though polling just 4.9% in the Aug 12 Socis survey and trailing Zelenskyy 20.7%-38.1% in a runoff. (5) Vitali Klitschko trims (0.18 -> 0.11) as a vocal Western-media critic of Zelenskyy's centralization, while Yulia Tymoshenko drops from the top 5 (absent from the Aug 12 Socis leaders and 2026 election coverage) into the 23% residual alongside Tymoshenko, Kyrylo Budanov, Dmytro Razumkov, Yulia Svyrydenko, and Ruslan Stefanchuk.
